title: MemoryDojo: Benchmarking Poisoning Through LLM Agent Memory
abstract: arXiv:2611.09721v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM agents benefit from using memory systems to improve performance on long-horizon, multi-session tasks. However, memory introduces a critical attack surface. Malicious instructions encountered in one session may be stored and propagated through memory before being retrieved and acted upon in later sessions. Because memory systems differ in how they process and retrieve information, the downstream effects of poisoning can vary significantly across systems. To quantify the effects of poisoning across different memory architectures, we introduce MemoryDojo, a benchmark for tracing the lifecycle of poisoned information through agent memory and measuring its influence on subsequent agent behavior. MemoryDojo is easily extensible, consists of 155 multi-session long-horizon trajectories covering four domains, and supports five different memory systems. translated_title: MemoryDojo：通过LLM智能体记忆对投毒攻击进行基准测试
translated_abstract: LLM智能体受益于使用记忆系统来提升其在长周期、多会话任务上的表现。然而，记忆也引入了一个关键的攻击面。在某个会话中遇到的恶意指令可能被存储并通过记忆传播，然后在后续会话中被检索并执行。由于不同的记忆系统在处理和检索信息的方式上存在差异，投毒攻击的下游影响在不同系统之间可能有显著不同。为了量化投毒在不同记忆架构中的影响，我们提出了MemoryDojo，这是一个用于追踪投毒信息在智能体记忆中生命周期、并衡量其对后续智能体行为影响的基准测试。MemoryDojo易于扩展，由覆盖四个领域的155条多会话长周期轨迹组成，并支持五种不同的记忆系统。通过评估，我们发现所有记忆系统都容易受到记忆投毒攻击。
tldr: 该论文提出了MemoryDojo基准测试，用于追踪和量化投毒信息在LLM智能体记忆系统中的传播及其对后续行为的影响，涵盖155条多会话轨迹、四个领域和五种记忆系统，并发现所有记忆系统均易受记忆投毒攻击。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces MemoryDojo, a benchmark for tracing the lifecycle of poisoned information through LLM agent memory and measuring its impact on subsequent behavior, covering 155 multi-session trajectories, four domains, and five memory systems, revealing that all memory systems are susceptible to memory poisoning.
